cues.en: who starts weird projects, and I'm sure that after Linux took over the operating system market and Git took over the distributed version control system market, subsurface will take over something. cues.en: Would you throw this away and and switch your toolkit? And I'll try to talk a little bit about the why and the how and the what and I'll Hopefully be able to explain and show you What a difference that the toolkit can make but the challenge of course was we had learned the hard way how to do GTK neither Linus nor I are UI developers
cues.zh: 你会把这一切都扔掉，然后更换你的工具包呢？我打算聊聊为什么、怎么做以及做什么，希望我能向大家解释并展示工具包能带来多么大的不同。但挑战当然在于，我们好不容易才搞懂了怎么写 GTK，而无论是 Linus 还是我都不是 UI 开发者。

The core developer community,
cues.zh: 它在这里显示出来了，很好。所以这是基于 GTK2 的。它看起来还算可以。我稍后会把它们并排展示。我们能够制作 Windows 二进制包、Mac 二进制包，当然也能在 Linux 发行版中从源码构建。GTK 的 Windows 支持和 Mac 支持有一些问题。核心开发者社区，

cues.zh: 很明显不认为这相关、重要或受支持。所以有一些子社区尝试让它工作，并取得不同程度成功。外观和感觉绝对不是原生的。我是说，连接近原生都算不上。而且你会遇到很多 bug，以及很多莫名其妙、无法解释的行为。

cues.en: We were at the point where people were saying, oh, this would be a great feature if somebody else would do the UI component. Because no one on the team was willing to deal with changes to the UI anymore. The complexity of doing this, the fragility, the fact that the model system was utterly broken the way it's designed was very, very frustrating. And there were lots of things we wanted to do differently, lots of just...
cues.zh: 我们当时到了这种地步：人们会说，哦，如果别人来做 UI 组件，这会是个很棒的功能。因为团队里没人愿意再处理 UI 的改动了。做这件事的复杂性、脆弱性，以及模型系统按那种方式设计完全是坏掉的事实，都非常非常令人沮丧。而且有很多事情我们想换个做法，很多只是……

cues.en: user interaction changes that we wanted and we could not find anybody who would help us implement it and we couldn't figure it out and the documentation is What's the polite word for terrible? I think terrible. Yeah But the biggest challenge for me and and and I say this I've said this to these people in person and I'll say it here again The biggest challenge for me with GTK is the attitude of the core community
cues.zh: 我们想要的用户交互改动，我们找不到任何人帮我们实现，我们自己也想不明白，而文档——terrible 的礼貌说法是什么？我觉得就是 terrible。是的。但对我来说最大的挑战，而且我——我当面对这些人说过，这里再说一遍：我用 GTK 最大的挑战是核心社区的态度

cues.en: The core community will tell you, if you have a problem, they will tell you A. Now that I can't repeat, I was just reminded of the politeness rules for this conference. The second thing they tell you is, you're doing it wrong. The third thing they're telling you, oh you don't get our vision, and then they stop talking to you. Because obviously that's all the help you need. It is utterly impossible to go with a concrete question saying your documentation states,
cues.zh: 核心社区会告诉你，如果你有问题，他们会告诉你 A。这个我现在不能重复，我刚想起来这个会议的礼貌规则。他们告诉你的第二件事是，你做错了。第三件事是，哦，你不懂我们的愿景，然后就不跟你说话了。因为显然这就是你需要的全部帮助。你根本不可能带着一个具体问题去说，你们的文档写着，

cues.en: This is what it should do. If I write exactly this code, it doesn't work. This is what it does. How do I get to working code? There is no way to get an answer to this. The only thing you can get is abuse. You can get long flame wars. So if you want lots of comments on your Google Plus posts, that works. So, by the way, beautiful fish. Poisonous. All these pictures are pictures that I took since...
cues.zh: 它应该做这个。如果我完全照这段代码写，它不工作。它实际做的是这个。我怎么才能得到能工作的代码？根本没办法得到答案。你能得到的只有辱骂。你可以得到长长的骂战。所以，如果你想在你的 Google Plus 帖子下得到很多评论，那倒有效。顺便说，漂亮的鱼。有毒。所有这些照片都是我自从……拍的。

cues.en: my last presentation here, and this one actually was taken on Lord Howe Island. This lionfish was, there were lots of them. They're really beautiful. So our issue with GTK was we tried for more than a year. We had engaged with a lot of Gnome and GTK developers, and we had come to the conclusion a year ago, this isn't worth it. We're gonna change, we're gonna try QT.
cues.zh: 这是我上次在这里演讲的照片，其实是在豪勋爵岛拍的。这种狮子鱼当时特别多，真的很漂亮。我们用 GTK 遇到的问题是，我们尝试了一年多，与很多 Gnome 和 GTK 的开发者沟通过，一年前我们得出结论：这根本不值得。我们要换，我们打算试试 QT。

cues.en: And when I talked about this in Canberra at this presentation, it's very interesting because I obviously got the required amount of flames from the GTK people, and I got a tremendous amount of enthusiasm from QT people. People walking up to me right there, I'm gonna help you, I'm gonna work with you. Now, of course, developers, being developers, everyone wants to help. The number of people who actually have the time to help, not so big.
cues.zh: 当我在堪培拉的那场演讲中聊到这事时，非常有意思，我显然遭到了 GTK 圈子里预料之中的口诛笔伐，但同时也收获了 QT 圈子极其巨大的热情。当时就有人走过来对我说：“我来帮你，我和你一起搞。”当然，开发者嘛，大家都想帮忙，但真正有时间帮忙的人其实并不多。

cues.en: the attitude in the QT community is fundamentally the opposite. So when you say something doesn't work, the answer is not unprintable and then you're doing it wrong. The answer is, oh, that's sad. Can I help you? Explain to me what you're trying to do. Oh, have you tried this thing? Have you tried that? And oh, by the way, they have documentation. They have documentation for application authors. And if you...
cues.zh: QT 社区的态度有着根本性的不同。当你反馈某个东西用不了时，他们给出的回答不是一句骂人的脏话外加“你用错了”。他们的回答是：“噢，太遗憾了，我能帮你吗？跟我说说你想做什么？噢，你试过这个吗？试过那个了吗？”顺便提一句，他们还有文档。他们为应用程序开发者准备了文档，如果你……

cues.en: tell them something, the documentation says this, and your software does this, they will fix it. So they either fix the documentation or the software. But the approach that this community has to someone who's trying to use their software is fundamentally different. And the other thing that was very encouraging to us is, as I said, the volunteers that came out. Some disappeared, some did.
cues.zh: 跟他们说：文档上是这么写的，但你们的软件表现却是那样，他们就会去修复。他们要么改文档，要么修软件。这个社区对待那些尝试使用他们软件的人的态度，有着本质的不同。另一件让我们非常受鼓舞的事，正如我刚才所说，是那些主动站出来的志愿者。有些人后来没音讯了，有些人确实帮了忙。

cues.en: doesn't commit to help get us started, and then they're not diverse, they disappeared. We had one volunteer, Thomas, who doesn't dive. Well, he now actually got certified a few weeks ago. But who has done about 80% of the grunt work of porting this? In his spare time...
cues.zh: 他们提交了代码帮我们起步，后来因为他们不潜水，也就离开了。我们有一位志愿者叫 Thomas，他以前不潜水——好吧，其实他几周前刚刚考了潜水证——但正是他在业余时间完成了移植工作中大约 80% 的脏活累活。

cues.en: just because he loves working on QT and he liked to encourage projects to use QT. Of course, as a side effect of all this engagement, he now has a job at Intel, but that's a different story. I keep telling people, if you're an active open source developer and you're unemployed, that's because you want to be unemployed.
cues.zh: 纯粹是因为他热爱用 QT 开发，并且喜欢鼓励其他项目使用 QT。当然，参与这一切的副产物就是，他现在在 Intel 找到了一份工作，不过那是另一个故事了。我总跟人说，如果你是一名活跃的开源开发者却处于失业状态，那纯粹是因为你自己想失业。

cues.en: There are so many jobs for good people. We are desperately looking for good people. And so is everybody else in this industry. So yeah, being active, being a volunteer, helping projects is a great way to find the job. What I like about Qt and what immediately was wonderful is it has very, very strong basic data structures. A lot of easy things are really easy. A lot of the...
cues.zh: 优秀的人有太多的工作机会，我们求贤若渴，这个行业的其他人也是如此。所以，保持活跃、做志愿者、帮助开源项目，是找工作极好的途径。对于 Qt，我喜欢的且立刻觉得很棒的一点是，它拥有极其强大的基础数据结构。很多简单的事情变得非常容易，很多……

cues.en: the basics of developing software. Linus and I are both C programmers. And I think Linus is on record how much he loves C++. Google for it if you don't get my drift. But nonetheless, with Qt, a lot of the ugliness of C++ is hidden from you. You can avoid a lot of the...
cues.zh: 开发软件的基础知识。Linus 和我都是 C 程序员。我记得 Linus 公开说过他有多喜欢 C++。不明白我意思的话可以自己搜一下。但尽管如此，用 Qt 能帮你隐藏掉 C++ 的很多丑陋之处。你可以避开很多……

cues.en: other insanity, and there's lots of other insanity in C++, and you can get a lot of things done very quickly, very easily. I think if we hadn't had volunteers help us who truly understand how Qt works, how a Qt application is supposed to act, how you should separate your logic
cues.zh: 其他离谱的东西，C++ 里离谱的东西可不少，而且你能非常快、非常轻松地完成很多事情。我觉得，如果没有那些真正理解 Qt 如何工作、Qt 应用应该如何表现、应该如何把逻辑

cues.en: from your UI code, how the signal slots, the callbacks, all this works. It would have been very, very hard. And I think, to be honest with you, when I started on this a year ago, I underestimated the challenge. But with the tremendous help from the Qt community, it actually wasn't that bad. It took a while. I mean, this is a reasonably sized UI project. So to get to feature parity took us
cues.zh: 和 UI 代码分开、信号槽和回调这一切如何运作的志愿者来帮我们，那会非常非常困难。老实说，一年前我开始做这个时，低估了挑战。但在 Qt 社区的巨大帮助下，其实还没那么糟。花了一段时间。我的意思是，这是一个规模不小的 UI 项目。所以要做到功能对齐，我们花了

cues.en: About six months, we started using it for our own diving in the summer. So in August, September, I was able to do the things that I want to do with the Qt version. And this is important. You need to use your own software, which is what the evolution people really should do. You need to use your own software so you see the problems that people have, so you can start commiserate with your users.
cues.zh: 大约六个月，夏天我们开始把它用于自己的潜水。所以在八月、九月，我就能用 Qt 版本做我想做的事了。这很重要。你需要使用自己的软件，这也是 evolution 的人真正应该做的。你需要使用自己的软件，才能看到人们遇到的问题，才能开始体谅你的用户。

cues.en: Let's see. Not everything is pretty when it comes to QT. Not everything is pretty when you migrate a project to QT. C++. Written and designed by monkeys on crack. On a lot of crack. cues.zh: 我看看。说到 Qt，并不是一切都美好。把项目迁移到 Qt 时，也不是一切都美好。C++。由嗑药的猴子编写和设计。嗑了很多药。这么说会冒犯吗，我能说嗑药吗？说非法药物吧，就说非法药物。我不想惹麻烦。

cues.en: I don't want to get in trouble. Pretty monkeys, troubled monkeys, troubled monkeys, good looking troubled monkeys apparently, but troubled. Compile times go up dramatically.
cues.zh: 我不想惹麻烦。漂亮的猴子，有麻烦的猴子，有麻烦的猴子，显然是长得好看但又有麻烦的猴子，但确实有麻烦。是啊是啊，来自非常糟糕的家庭，算了。所以 C++ 除了设计上的疯狂和语言规范里的那些胡言乱语之外，还带来几个问题。编译时间会急剧上升。

cues.en: So we were able, if I built the GDK version and the Qt version, it's like a factor of five in how long it takes me to compile. For most developers, that's not a big deal because make system is reasonably clever to only recompile what you need to recompile, but if you're the maintainer, so after every commit you try to rebuild everything, you rebuild it on three platforms, it's pretty noticeable for me.
cues.zh: 所以如果我们构建 GDK 版本和 Qt 版本，我编译所需时间的差距大概是五倍。对大多数开发者来说这不算什么，因为 make 系统还算聪明，只会重新编译需要重新编译的东西；但如果你是维护者，每次提交后都要尝试重新构建所有东西，还要在三个平台上重建，那对我来说就非常明显了。

cues.en: Speaking of build systems, for the GTK version, we had a beautiful handcrafted makefile that I believe not a single person in our team actually understood. And that did magical things. Oh, I forgot to mention this.
cues.zh: 说到构建系统，GTK 版本我们有一个漂亮的手写 makefile，我相信我们团队里没有一个人真正看懂它。它做了些神奇的事情。后来 Tiago 让我们改用 QMake，这就很无聊了，因为你居然能搞懂它在干什么，而且它在所有平台上都能用，太奇怪了。非常令人失望。哦，我忘了提这个。

cues.en: I forget to mention this earlier. One of the big advantages that we had in our QT migration is Tiago Macieira. He's the QT core maintainer, and he's actually a coworker and a friend of mine. So often we ran into problems and was like, hey Tiago, what do I do now? And either he knew how to fix it or he knew...
cues.zh: 我刚才忘了提这一点。我们在向 QT 迁移时的巨大优势之一，就是 Tiago Macieira。他是 QT 的核心维护者，也是我的同事兼朋友。他虽然不潜水，但因为和我共事，人非常好，偶尔会帮帮我们，更重要的是能帮我们引荐对的人。所以每当我们遇到问题，就会问：“嘿，Tiago，我现在该怎么办？”他要么知道怎么解决，要么知道……

cues.en: whom to ask, whom to get engaged. So local knowledge, having someone in the team who is connected with the community was a huge advantage. But back to the things that I dislike about QT. The model and view system in GTK is completely broken. The model and view system in QT is pretty much completely broken.
cues.zh: 该去问谁、该找谁帮忙。所以，这种本土化的认知，团队里能有个深入社区的人，真是一个巨大的优势。但言归正传，聊聊我不喜欢 QT 的地方。GTK 的模型-视图系统简直烂透了；QT 的模型-视图系统也基本烂透了。

cues.en: I don't think anybody has figured out a simple, easy to use system where you have your data structures and you can project them into a view that you can manipulate in a consistent way and that makes sense. The biggest challenge on the QT side is the verbosity of all this. So the amount of boilerplate that you need to write, the amount of functions and functions and more functions that call each other,
cues.zh: 我觉得根本没人搞出过一套简单易用的系统，能让你把手头的数据结构，以合理且一致的方式映射并操作在视图上。QT 这边最大的挑战就是太冗长繁琐了。你必须写大量的样板代码，还有无数互相调用的函数、函数、再加函数，

It's an interaction with the end user. It doesn't matter if it takes 200 cycles longer. Anyway, so the
cues.zh: 你就会意识到，大多数人一开始并不是多么厉害的开发者。即便他们技术很牛，通常也是写内核代码的。奇怪的是，面向终端用户的应用和内核完全是两码事。所以每当 Linus 跟我说“哎呀，那样写效率太低了”的时候，我就想：是啊，但这不是内核啊。这是和终端用户的交互，多花 200 个周期根本无所谓。不管怎么说，

cues.en: You have no idea. Having a brilliant developer on your team is awesome. Having a brilliant developer on your team who A, started the project and B, is opinionated like Linus, can be challenging.
cues.zh: 你根本想象不到。团队里有个顶尖的开发者固然很棒；但如果这个顶尖开发者既是项目的发起人，又像 Linus 那样极有主见，那可就非常具有挑战性了。

cues.en: Once you've gone through this whole process of trying to separate out, this is how I display things, this is how I do the math, how do the logic, how it's supposed to work. The second big challenge is that in the re-implementation, you separate out from here the things where we didn't get what we wanted because we couldn't get it to work.
cues.zh: 当你完成了整个分离过程，分清了“这里负责界面展示”、“这里负责数学计算和逻辑处理，负责它的预期运作方式”之后，第二个大挑战就是：在重新实现时，把那些因为没搞定而没达到预期效果的部分剥离出来，

cues.en: From oh, this works as intended don't change it. So I keep showing this this Audity that we can't edit in place and I know this is possible in GTK. We just weren't able to make it work So you have to do the double click and you get the weird window Of course, you don't want to re-implement something like this in QT on the other hand We absolutely love the way our profile looked and we want to make sure that under
cues.zh: 区别于“噢，这个功能符合预期，千万别改动”。比如我总拿这个奇怪的现象举例：我们当时无法就地编辑，而我知道在 GTK 里是能做到的，只是我们没能调通。所以你必须双击，然后会弹出一个奇怪的窗口。在 QT 里你当然不想再搞出这种东西了；但另一方面，我们又非常喜欢潜水剖面图现有的显示样式，希望能确保在……

cues.en: this looks very much the same way. So you need to separate out on your UI code what is the functionality that I actually want or that I want to make tiny improvements to. For example, if you look at the overlay display. So here you can just move the overlay around and it stays where it is, stays put, and it shows you the additional information for wherever your mouse cursor is versus in GTK this is a tool tip and it
cues.zh: 在新的实现下看起来基本一致。因此，你需要在 UI 代码中理清：哪些是我真正想要的功能，或者哪些只需做微调？比如看一下这个浮层显示：在这里你可以随意拖动浮层，它就会停在那里不动，并随着你的鼠标指针位置显示额外的信息；而在 GTK 中这是一个工具提示，它……

cues.en: That's random things, and I can never explain when it shows up and where it shows up and why it sometimes moves and sometimes doesn't. See, now it jumped. It's weird. So where do you want to make just small adjustments versus where do you want to use the strength of the new toolkit and implement things totally differently? So what I found worked extremely well for us was to have someone
cues.zh: 它总是乱来，我根本搞不懂它什么时候会出现、会出现在哪儿，以及为什么有时候会跟着动、有时候又不动。看，刚才就跳了一下，非常诡异。所以，到底哪些地方你只想做微调，而哪些地方你想利用新工具集的优势去彻底重构？我发现对我们非常有效的一个做法，就是找一个……

cues.en: who is very familiar with the new toolkit, with Qt, but isn't familiar with our application and not even with the use case. So someone who challenged me every step of the way, making me explain a what is it that I want, why do I want it this way and not another way, and constantly came with new ideas, oh we could do this, oh we could do that. Now, UI developers are interesting people and they have crazy ideas.
cues.zh: 对新工具集（也就是 Qt）非常熟悉，但对我们的应用甚至对具体使用场景都不了解的人。这样一个人可以在每一步都提出质疑，逼我解释清楚：第一，我想要的到底是什么？为什么非要这样实现而不是换种方式？并且他还会不断冒出新想法：“噢，我们可以这样做”、“噢，我们也可以那样做”。UI 开发者是一群很有意思的人，他们总是有各种天马行空的想法。

cues.en: There is often the reigning things in, yeah, no, we don't need to have this completely different, staying true to your vision, staying true to what you want your application to be. But at the same time, listening to all the great ideas of how things could be different. So if you see, for example, the amount of information that we are showing
cues.zh: 经常需要收着点，对，不，我们不需要把它做得完全不同，要忠于你的愿景，忠于你希望应用成为的样子。但与此同时，也要听取所有关于可以如何做得不同的好点子。所以比如你看，我们所展示的信息量

cues.en: in the dive nodes between the two applications has increased dramatically. So we're showing a lot more things in this one window because of the push from our UI developers to have less overlay secondary windows, additional things, and make things simpler, more...
cues.zh: 在两个应用的潜水节点中已经大幅增加。因为 UI 开发者推动减少叠加的次级窗口和额外元素，让界面更简单、更……

cues.en: in one place, fewer pop-ups, fewer additional dialogues. It's things like this. So it's very important to listen to the people with the experience and to find this balance of what do I want and what can I get done in a finite amount of time. So we had foolishly hoped to get...
cues.zh: 更集中在一处，更少弹窗，更少额外对话框。就是这类事情。所以倾听有经验的人非常重要，并在“我想要什么”和“有限时间内能完成什么”之间找到平衡。所以我们曾愚蠢地希望……

cues.en: I shouldn't say we, I should blame myself. I had foolishly hoped that from starting the work on QT in earnest in about early April, within about six months, yeah, come on, six months you can get this done, right? So I was hoping that by early fall I would be able to release Subsurface 4. And it actually took a tremendous effort by a few people through the month of December and many, many, many sleepless nights.
cues.zh: 我不该说“我们”，该怪我自己。我曾愚蠢地以为，大约四月初真正开始 QT 的工作后，六个月内——是啊，拜托，六个月你总能做完吧？所以我希望到初秋就能发布 Subsurface 4。而实际上，几个人在十二月整月付出了巨大努力，熬过无数个不眠之夜。

cues.en: to get this done. Fortunately I suffer from pretty bad insomnia with the result that very often between midnight and 4am I would be downstairs sitting on the computer working on subsurface instead of doing foolish things like sleeping. So we have of course more ideas what we want to do and things that we think are additional benefits that we can get from the migration to QT. One of the fun things with QT is what they've done with QML.
cues.zh: 才把它完成。幸运的是，我失眠相当严重，结果常常在午夜到凌晨四点之间，我会在楼下坐在电脑前做 Subsurface，而不是干睡觉这种傻事。当然，我们还有更多想做的点子，也认为从迁移到 QT 中能获得一些额外好处。QT 有意思的一点是他们对 QML 所做的工作。

cues.en: that you can create a descriptive way of doing your UI. And that allows you to trivially port your user interface to touch-based devices. QT and QML are supported under iOS, under Android, under Tizen, I think under BlackBerry, but who cares? So the ability to move this
cues.zh: 让你能用描述式方式构建 UI。这让你能轻松把用户界面移植到触屏设备。QT 和 QML 支持 iOS、Android、Tizen，我想还有 BlackBerry，但谁在乎呢？所以能够把这套东西

cues.en: to a tablet. Now, there are, of course, challenges. Phones and tablets tend to not have full USB stacks. A lot of these supporting libraries that we need for this to work aren't necessarily ported yet. So the biggest for us is libdive computer. I assume I should have asked in the beginning, do you guys even know what subsurface does?
cues.zh: 迁移到平板上。当然也有挑战。手机和平板往往没有完整的 USB 协议栈。很多让它工作所需的支持库还不一定已经移植。所以我们最大的难题是 libdivecomputer。我想我一开始就该问：你们到底知道 Subsurface 是做什么的吗？

cues.en: Guess I started in the middle. So what we do is you can download dive data from a dive computer and visualize it. But this download from a dive computer, this is, of course, a highly proprietary industry where everyone invents their own download standards. And it's extremely fragmented. So there is a library that is used by many different dive log programs, many commercial proprietary dive log programs called Lib Dive Computer.
cues.zh: 看来我是从中间开始讲的。我们做的是，你可以从潜水电脑下载潜水数据并将其可视化。但从潜水电脑下载数据，这当然是一个高度专有的行业，每个人都发明自己的下载标准。而且极其碎片化。所以有一个库被许多不同的潜水日志程序使用，很多商业专有潜水日志程序都用它，叫 Lib Dive Computer。

cues.en: that is at the core of what we do. So even if we move subsurface to a tablet or a phone, you still need to be able to have that library compile and work there and have the ability to connect your device. So you need host mode USB instead of just gadget mode USB.
cues.zh: 这是我们工作的核心。所以即使把 Subsurface 移植到平板或手机上，你也依然需要让那个库能在上面编译并运行，还得有连接设备的能力。也就是说，你需要 USB 主机模式，而不仅仅是从机设备模式。

cues.en: Other things that people want integration of, I mean, obviously I like the pictures that I do. Integration of pictures and video into the program. A lot more ability to mix statistics, mix information that you can gleam, data analysis that you can gleam from your past into the future. More support for technical divers, for crazy people who die diving rebreathers. No, who dive rebreathers, sorry.
cues.zh: 人们希望整合的其他功能，比如，我很喜欢自己拍的照片，也就是把图片和视频整合到程序中。还有更多融合统计数据的能力，融合能从过去挖掘出的信息，以及能推演到未来的数据分析。还有为技术潜水员提供更多支持，为那些玩密闭式呼吸器潜水的疯子们……不，是玩循环呼吸器的潜友，不好意思。

cues.en: Things like that, but right now we are super thrilled. We have a version out I I got it out. I think two weeks ago right before Christmas And I'm hopefully tonight releasing 402 because I in my excitement In included a very nice bug in the last one that on Windows causes freakin crashes But yeah that we have we have tons of ideas and as always more ideas than we have times and have developers working on this
cues.zh: 诸如此类的事，但现在我们非常激动。我们已经发布了一个版本，两周前圣诞节前夕我刚发出来。今晚我希望能发布 4.0.2 版，因为我之前太兴奋了，在上一版里引入了一个很棒的 bug，会导致在 Windows 上莫名其妙崩溃。不过是的，我们有很多想法，而且一如既往，想法总比我们的时间和投入的开发者多。

cues.en: And with that, questions? Oh, gosh. So I'm supposed to repeat what you said, Linus. The quick summary is, yeah, I know. The quick summary is, as I said earlier, in many cases, the things that we wanted to do may have been possible with GTK.
cues.zh: 说到这里，有提问吗？天呐。我得重复一下你刚才说的话，Linus。简要总结一下就是，对，我知道。简要总结就是，正如我之前所说，在很多情况下，我们想做的事情用 GTK 可能也是做得到的。

cues.en: We just couldn't figure out to make them work the way we wanted them to work. Linus gave the example of editing a text box. Yes, you can do that, but then your focus in the rest of the application doesn't work, and getting in and out is a real pain. But fundamentally, I am convinced that most everything that we've done in the Qt version would have been possible in GTK. It's just, if you are a group of hobbyists doing this for fun,
cues.zh: 我们只是没摸索出如何按我们期望的方式来实现。Linus 刚才举了编辑文本框的例子。是的，你能编辑，但应用程序其余部分的焦点就失效了，焦点的切入切出非常痛苦。但从根本上说，我确信我们在 Qt 版本里做的大多数事情，在 GTK 里本来也能做到。只是，如果你是一群出于兴趣做这个的业余爱好者，

cues.en: And you can't get any help in getting the development to do or the program to do what you want it to do. At some point, it's time to move on. Other questions? Yes. Yes. So the question is, my presentation was about how rewriting a UI can make it better and whether with the right people, if we could have done this in GTK3. My honest answer is no, I don't think so.
cues.zh: 而且在开发过程中得不到任何帮助来让程序达到预期的效果，那到了某个时候，就该换个方向了。还有其他问题吗？好的。好的。刚才的问题是：我的演讲是关于重写 UI 如何让它变得更好，以及如果有合适的人选，我们是否本可以用 GTK3 完成这一切？我的实话是：不，我觉得不能。

cues.en: Obviously, this is me as a private person, so this is not an Intel project. I can't just go to a coworker and say, I need you to work on this. And all attempts to get the many GNOME people at Intel to look at this and participate have utterly failed. We got a random patch here or there, but we were not able to get anyone involved. And when I asked why, they say, oh, I don't write applications, I write GNOME.
cues.zh: 显然，这只是我的个人行为，并不是 Intel 的项目。我不能直接去找同事说，我需要你来做这个。而且所有试图让 Intel 众多搞 GNOME 的人来看看并参与进来的尝试，全都彻底失败了。我们偶尔能收到一两个零散的补丁，但根本无法让任何人真正参与进来。每当我问为什么，他们就说：“噢，我不写应用程序，我写的是 GNOME。”

cues.en: I don't care. I don't know how to do this. We had three of the core gnome maintainers sit together and try and help me answer one of my questions. And they said, I have no idea how to do this. I never do this. So the fundamental issue is not that I think it's not possible to do this in GDK. It's that no one knows how to do it. It's not documented. And there is no easy way to get this help. That was the challenge why we moved away.
cues.zh: 我不在乎。我不知道这怎么做。我们让三位 Gnome 核心维护者坐在一起，试着帮我回答我的一个问题。他们说：我完全不知道怎么做。我从没这么做过。所以根本问题不是我认为 GDK 做不到。而是没人知道怎么做。没有文档。也没有简单办法获得这种帮助。这就是我们离开的挑战。

cues.en: But this is not an Intel policy question. This is not an endorsement or anything. This is an open source project that I happen to maintain in my spare time, usually at night. And this is our experience. Karen. OK. So the question is if we got great help in the QT community because Linus is famous. Well, so A, Linus was famous when he worked on GTK.
cues.zh: 但这不是 Intel 的政策问题。这不是背书或任何东西。这是我碰巧在业余时间、通常晚上维护的一个开源项目。这是我们的经历。Karen。好。所以问题是，如果我们在 Qt 社区得到了很大帮助，是因为 Linus 很有名。嗯，第一，Linus 在做 GTK 时就已经很有名了。

cues.en: And that didn't help us. But to answer your actual question, yes, I've talked to a bunch of other projects who have recently migrated from GTK to QTE or who have started to work on QTE. And in general, the response from most of the application developers is that the QTE community is very, very open to questions. And I think...
cues.zh: 但这没帮到我们。不过回答你真正的问题，是的，我和一群其他项目聊过，他们最近从 GTK 迁移到 Qt，或者开始用 Qt。总的来说，大多数应用开发者的反馈是，Qt 社区非常非常欢迎提问。而且我觉得……

cues.en: Okay, now I'm assigning intent, and please correct me if I'm wrong. But my perception is that the Gnome and GTK developers see development of Gnome as their goal, and GTK as the toolkit to do that, and that is their focus. And there seems to be very little focus on other people trying to develop applications.
cues.zh: 好，现在我在推测意图，如果我错了请纠正我。但我的感觉是，Gnome 和 GTK 开发者把开发 Gnome 视为目标，把 GTK 视为实现它的工具包，这就是他们的重点。而他们似乎很少关注其他想开发应用的人。

cues.en: On the other side, QT came from the Trolltech days. So this was a company that made their living in consulting two ISVs who then wrote applications. So their whole focus has been great documentation for people who want to use their toolkit, a good way of interacting with them, of getting the information out to them. And oh, by the way, KDE, well, the counterpart to Gnome in this comparison, right?
cues.zh: 另一边，Qt 来自 Trolltech 时代。所以这是一家靠给两家 ISV 做咨询为生的公司，这两家 ISV 随后写应用。所以他们整个重点一直是：为想用他们工具包的人提供好文档，提供良好的互动方式，把信息传递给他们。哦对了，KDE，在这个比较里是 Gnome 的对应物，对吧？

cues.en: KDE was completely disjoint from this. KDE was just another set of applications that happened to use Qt. And I see a lot less overlap in the developers between the KDE people and the Qt people, and a lot more interest in people who are just writing an average app. And oh, by the way, in the GTK world, the whole idea that
cues.zh: KDE 与此完全不相干。KDE 只是另一组碰巧使用 Qt 的应用。我看到 KDE 人和 Qt 人之间的开发者重叠少得多，而对只是写普通应用的人兴趣大得多。哦对了，在 GTK 世界里，整个想法是——

cues.en: You might not actually be running this on Debian as the main platform, but you might be, oh my gosh, on Windows. There is a lot of hostility towards any problems that you report that happen because you're trying to do this on Mac or on Windows. Yet, if you write a program for a diver, while we have, I mean, who in this room is a diver? Yeah, we have a few open source divers, but
cues.zh: 你可能实际上并不是在 Debian 上把它作为主平台运行，而可能是在——我的天——Windows 上。对于你因为在 Mac 或 Windows 上尝试这么做而报告的任何问题，都有很多敌意。然而，如果你为潜水员写程序，虽然我们有——我是说，这个房间里有谁是潜水员？对，我们有几个开源潜水员，但是

cues.en: But the vast majority of our users are on Windows and Mac. And actually, the fact that we have Linux as a developer distorts this. So we have about 65% Windows, 20% Mac, and 15% Linux. And if Linux wasn't one of the developers, we'd have 2% Linux. I guarantee you that. And so in the QT community,
cues.zh: 但我们绝大多数用户在 Windows 和 Mac 上。而实际上，我们让 Linux 作为开发者之一，这一点扭曲了数据。所以我们大约 65% 是 Windows，20% 是 Mac，15% 是 Linux。如果 Linux 不是开发者之一，我们只有 2% 的 Linux。我向你保证。所以在 Qt 社区，

cues.en: Working on Mac, working on Windows is a core goal. If it doesn't work there, it is broken. But you do not have that on the GDK side at all. Did I miss your signal? I'm sorry, I was...
cues.zh: 在 Mac 上工作、在 Windows 上工作是核心目标。如果在这些平台上不能用，那就是坏了。但在 GDK 这边你完全没有这一点。我是不是错过了你的信号？抱歉，我刚才……
